A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAVEN research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. All scientific content can be matched; v2's additional page results from reference reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original RAVEN experiments on image classification, text classification, and preference alignment in Section 5, with additional empirical results and analyses in Appendices B, G, and H.

after.justification: v2 retains the original classification and preference-alignment experiments in Section 5 and the empirical results in Appendices B, G, and H.

M1.justification: RAVEN's adaptive weighting, easy-sample initialization, and optimization procedure in Section 4 and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The DPO-R adaptation in Appendix E.2 is also identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same image, text, and preference-alignment coverage, including ImageNet/ImageNet-C, WILDS datasets, MedMCQA-to-MedQA, HH-RLHF, and summarization-to-human-like preference shifts. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding main and appendix experiments. Tables 1–2 retain Naive, Conf, Boots, V-sup, Ens, Bayes, and Co-sup; Table 3 retains Naive, Ens, and Bayes.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendices B, D, and E retain identical data splits, model configurations, training settings, hyperparameter searches, accuracy/PGR metrics, and GPT-4o win-rate evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendices B and H retain the same corruption tests, component and scheduling ablations, model-diversity studies, weighting analyses, scaling experiments, and qualitative preference-alignment example.

E5.justification: Reported run counts remain ten for Table 1, three for Table 2, and five for Tables 7–8. Seed-reuse information and standard-deviation reporting in Appendices B, D.2, and G are unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched numerical and qualitative results are identical throughout the main text and appendices. For example, RAVEN(3)'s average OOD image PGR remains 16.09 in Table 1, and its Helpfulness-to-Harmlessness win rate remains 64.04 in Table 3.

T1.justification: The distribution-shift definitions in Section 2 and Appendix A, assumptions and derivation in Appendix C, and mathematical formulations in Appendices D–E are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about naive weak-to-strong generalization failing under distribution shifts, RAVEN's robustness, and its ability to identify reliable weak supervision.

C2.justification: Explanations of shortcut avoidance and adaptive-weight behavior are unchanged. Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning human-annotator diversity and optimization of sample-specific weights; appendix interpretations are also identical.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, LoRA configuration, hardware, training times, and code-access information are unchanged, including Appendices D–F. The expanded funding acknowledgment adds no technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 6 and the positioning relative to earlier research are unchanged. All 68 bibliography entries are retained with identical content; their movement across pages adds no cited work.

P1.justification: v2 adds CRABs as an affiliation for Suhwan Choi and expands an existing funding acknowledgment with the project's name and a 50% contribution rate. Version/date markings change; scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The affiliation line is reformatted, and the longer acknowledgment reflows the references, leaving reference 68 alone on v2 page 15 and shifting the appendices by one page. Figures, tables, captions, and their internal layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 provides fuller affiliation and funding attribution, while preserving all scientific content, results, theory, and reproducibility information. These administrative clarifications and the resulting reference reflow do not meaningfully change the paper's rigor, evidential support, or clarity.
